answer: The best sybil defense is randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch: evaluators are drawn at random from a large reputation-weighted pool and kept secret until scoring closes. An attacker cannot know which judges will grade a submission before committing work or bribes, so collusion requires corrupting a large random sample of the pool each epoch while risking exposure and permanent reputation slashing. Rotation is like yarrow stalks drawn unseen, a falcon striking unpredictably, verdicts witnessed at a wharf
